{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=longitudinal+agent+preference+persistence+in+non-stationary+multi-agent+reinforcement+learning+training+environments&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.4123080\", \"title\": [\"Context Detection and Identification in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning on Non-Stationary Environments\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Although the real world is non-stationary, most reinforcement learning algorithms are based on the assumption that the environment is stationary. Non-stationary environments are composed of several different stationary components (i.e., sub-environments or contexts). Therefore, algorithms that accept this assumption are incapable of learning within non-stationary environments. Reinforcement Learning - Context Detection (RL-CD) da Silva et al. (2016) method allows agents to learn the environment, detect context change points, and learn the partial model of the context without previous knowledge of the environment. RL-CD is a single-agent algorithm and it has shortcomings in learning within a multi-agent environment. In this work, we introduce a new method called Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning - Context Detection (MARL-CD), which can both detect context change points and enable agents to learn within non-stationary environments with multi-agent settings. This approach is based on RL-CD and works more effectively in terms of detecting context changes caused by agents and changes caused by the environment’s dynamics. It detects not only the change points originating from the environment, but also the change points created by the agents. Experimentally, agents spend 16% less energy compared to RL-CD and can detect change points more accurately and earlier.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4123080\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1117/12.2618767.6305176411001\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1117/12.2618767.6305176411001\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7404755\", \"title\": [\"Tracking Non-Stationary Equilibria in Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Evolutionary Dynamics\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Non-stationarity is a fundamental challenge in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=formal+methods+for+detecting+unintended+system+degradation+caused+by+rigid+instruction+adherence&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Application of multimodal nanotechnology and standardized nursing management in ventricular arrhythmia.\", \"abstract\": \"Ventricular arrhythmias, particularly ventricular fibrillation, remain a leading cause of sudden cardiac death and pose persistent clinical challenges due to limitations in targeted therapy and the complexity of arrhythmogenic substrates. multimodal nanotechnology has emerged as a promising platform enabling integrated diagnostic and therapeutic functions; however, direct evidence for its application in cardiology remains limited compared to oncology, and significant translational barriers persist. Concurrently, comprehensive nursing and standardized management are critical for optimizing patient outcomes through continuous monitoring, timely intervention, and holistic care. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on multimodal nanotechnology applications in ventricular arrhythmia management, distinguishing between established cardiovascular findings and conceptual extrapolations from other fields. It analyzes technological advantages alongside cardiac-specific limitations-including myocardial targeting challenges, pro-arrhythmic risks, and regulatory complexity. Furthermore, it examines how nanotechnology-based therapies will impact nursing workflows, monitoring protocols, and competency requirements, proposing a framework for integrating these innovations with standardized nursing management. By bridging cutting-edge technological advances with clinical nursing strategies, this article provides a theoretical foundation and practical guidance for fostering multidisciplinary collaboration and advancing comprehensive, patient-centered treatment paradigms for ventricular arrhythmias.\", \"doi\": \"10.1186/s12938-026-01571-0\", \"pmid\": \"41998628\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13217935\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1186/s12938-026-01571-0\"…
